title: SUM: add a range
objectives: Use SUM to total a group of cells.
Choose a range that includes every relevant row.
about: SUM adds the values in one or more cells. A colon between two cell references includes every cell in the range.

examples.why: The range includes all three amounts.
SUM works across a row as well as down a column.

watch_out: Check both ends of the range; missing the last row gives a plausible but incorrect total.
Text and blank cells are ignored by SUM.
recap: Use SUM with a colon-separated range to total cells. The correct range matters just as much as the function.

steps.prompt: In B6, total every daily sale from B2 through B5 using SUM.
hints: The daily sales run from B2 to B5.
steps.explanation: The colon includes every cell from B2 through B5, so the total updates when any sale changes.

common_mistakes.message: That stops at Wednesday. Include Thursday in B5.
That range includes the header. Start with the first sale in B2.
The total is right today, but type a SUM formula so it updates when a sale changes.

steps.prompt: In C7, calculate the combined units for the six stores in C2:C6 and C8.
hints: Include all six store values, not the blank result cell.
The data starts at C2 and ends at C6; C8 is also a store value.
steps.explanation: SUM can combine a continuous range and a separate cell in one formula.

common_mistakes.message: That leaves out the final store value in C8.
That range includes the answer cell C7. Add C8 separately instead.
Your first range stops one store too soon. Include C6.

steps.prompt: In D6, total the North-region sales in D2:D5.
hints: Use the visible North sales values in D2 and D4.
A SUM formula can take more than one argument.
steps.explanation: SUM accepts individual cell references when the values to add are not in one continuous range.

common_mistakes.message: That includes the South and East values. Add only the North sales.
The arithmetic works, but this exercise asks you to use SUM.
That also includes the South sale in D3. Leave it out.
